title: Cheetah, leopard or jaguar?

scenes.headline: Solid spots + tear lines
scenes.body: Solid round or oval spots, and a black line from each eye to the mouth.

scenes.headline: Rosettes with empty centres
scenes.body: Smaller rosettes packed close together, with no dot inside.

scenes.headline: Big rosettes, dot in the middle
scenes.body: Larger, blockier rosettes that often have small spots inside.

scenes.headline: Easiest clue: the map
scenes.body: Jaguars: only the Americas. Leopards: Africa and Asia. Wild cheetahs: mostly Africa.

caption:
Three spotted cats, three different patterns.

A small population of Asiatic cheetahs survives in Iran and is critically endangered, which is why we say 'mostly Africa'.

Source: Smithsonian's National Zoo; National Geographic. Photos/video: Wikimedia Commons (credits on screen).
notes: Classic save-worthy ID reel; the comparison plate plus single-species close-ups give a clue per scene. Original: our checklist and order, not a reposted chart.
